Subject: Quick recap + DPA / SCC clarification items from today

Hi Emma,

Great to speak earlier — appreciate the level of detail you shared about BrightHealth's data flows. As promised, a short recap and suggested next steps so procurement and security have a clean intake: 

Summary from call:
- Primary use case: clinical triage assistant for member support; PII/PHI will be plaintext in inputs in scoped flows.
- Compliance drivers: HIPAA for US PHI, plus GDPR obligations for EU members.
- Timeline: target pilot in early Q4 (3–6 week security intake preferred).

Immediate asks we discussed:
1) Copy of your VSQ / procurement form — Ben can kick off the questionnaire from our side.
2) SOC 2: BrightHealth asked whether Redwood has a current SOC 2 report and whether we can provide a redacted copy.
3) DPA + SCC module: Need to confirm which SCC module BrightHealth prefers for EU transfers (Module 1 vs Module 2) and whether you will take the controller role for all processing or request a hybrid mapping for analytics/auditing.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben will share the vendor security questionnaire to your procurement inbox (procurement@brighthealth.com).
- Marissa will attach our DPA template and SCC module matrix and outline the standard controller/processor language we use for customers with HIPAA+GDPR requirements.
- Emma / procurement to confirm: (a) preferred SCC module and (b) whether BrightHealth will be Controller for all customer data, or if you need Redwood to be Controller for certain internal telemetry.

I'll add these to the HubSpot deal and share a Drive link. If that sounds right, we'll aim to have the VSQ returned in 5–7 business days and plan a legal follow-up once procurement confirms SCC preference.

Thanks — speak soon.

Jonas Weber

Subject: Re: Quick recap + DPA / SCC clarification items from today

Emma — thanks again. Two quick notes from Legal/Privacy perspective I wanted to surface: 

1) DPA template: our standard DPA assumes BrightHealth is the Controller and Redwood is the Processor for member data submitted to the inference API. For telemetry and platform health metrics we typically include a narrow processor role for Redwood (we capture aggregate, non-identifiable usage unless specifically enabled). If you have analytics workflows that require Redwood to act as Controller for derived datasets, flag those so Legal can review.

2) SCC module recommendation: For most health-tech customers transferring limited data cross-border on the standard contract, Module 1 (Controller-to-Controller) is not appropriate because Redwood acts as a Processor. We typically propose Module 2 (Controller-to-Processor) variants, but I understand some customers prefer a Module 1-style mapping when they ingest data into a customer-managed environment. Please confirm whether BrightHealth expects Redwood to host EU member data in Redwood-managed infrastructure (hosted mode) or to route to a Europe-dedicated private deployment (Dedicated/Private). That choice affects SCC module text and liability carve-outs.

What Marissa can provide right away:
- Redacted SOC 2 (Type II) report (we can provide an NDA-guarded copy).
- Redwood DPA template (attached) with Module 2 recommended text and a short options table for Module 2 vs Module 3.

If useful, we can prepare a short two-page write-up: "Recommended SCC module and controller/processor roles for BrightHealth" that maps your described flows to suggested contract language.

Marissa Cole
Security & Compliance Liaison | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Thanks, team — clear recap. A few clarifications from our side after internal review: 

- SOC 2: We need a redacted Type II report and a point of contact for follow-up questions. If you can share under an NDA, procurement will circulate it to our security reviewers.
- SCC module: Our legal prefers Module 2 (Controller-to-Processor) given Redwood will process member inputs on your hosted infra.
- Controller mapping: BrightHealth will act as Controller for member-submitted data. However, for some aggregated analytics that our Data Science team will request (anonymized usage trends), we may want Redwood to provide de-identified datasets — we expect Redwood to remain Processor in that case.

Procurement note (procurement@brighthealth.com): please confirm an NDA and routing for the SOC2. Girish from procurement (cc'd) will own the return of the VSQ.

Can you also confirm the expected time to produce a DPA redline once we confirm Module 2? We are aiming to finalize legal terms before the pilot kickoff window.

—Emma
